name: Close authentication path coverage gaps
description: Enumerate every route into the in-scope environment, bring each under central authentication policy, and give any route that genuinely cannot be covered a documented, monitored compensating control.
responsible_role: IT / Identity and Access Management owner

steps.action: Enumerate all authentication paths into the boundary: SSO, direct application logins, VPN, SSH and bastion, cloud console, cloud CLI, API and personal access tokens, break-glass accounts, and vendor support portals.
Classify each path as covered, coverable, or structurally uncoverable.
Migrate coverable paths behind the identity provider and enforce the second factor through conditional access policy.
For structurally uncoverable paths, implement compensating controls: credential vaulting, short-lived credentials, network restriction, and alerting on use.
Record every exclusion with an owner, rationale, compensating control, and review date.
Prefer phishing-resistant factors for administrative and privileged access.
Reconcile the policy document and the system description to the configuration actually enforced.
Capture dated configuration snapshots on a schedule so period coverage can be demonstrated, not just current state.

implementation_considerations: Path enumeration should be done by someone other than the person who configured the policy; self-review reliably misses the same paths twice.
Legacy applications that cannot sit behind the identity provider drive the timeline. Decide early whether to retire, wrap, or compensate them.
Phishing-resistant factors change enrolment logistics and hardware procurement; sequence that ahead of enforcement.
typical_duration: Weeks to months, driven by migrating legacy applications and token-based access rather than by policy configuration.
prerequisites: A current and accurate system boundary definition
An identity provider capable of fronting the applications in scope

verification_method.how: Re-enumerate authentication paths independently of the original list and confirm each is either covered by enforced policy or appears on the documented exclusion list with a live compensating control.

residual_risk_note: Newly integrated applications and newly issued long-lived tokens reintroduce uncovered paths. Without a control at the point of onboarding, coverage decays.
period_limitation_note: Closing a coverage gap now does not change the design conclusion for a period during which the gap existed.
notes: Framed as closing coverage of the criterion's objective. MFA is not a SOC 2 requirement, and an organization may meet CC6.1 through a different design.
Backfilled with responsible_role and implementation_considerations in the CC6 phase (schema 0.2.0).
